8.1.6 Economic importance of Plasmodium Plasmodium vivax has no any harmful effect inside the body of Anopheles but it is pathogenic to human being causing a disease, Benign tertian malaria. The symptoms in the case of P.vivax appear after 14 days of initial infection. This time is utilized by the parasite to establish malarial symptoms. For this, large number of parasites continues their life cycle in the RBCs. When all the schizonts in RBC burst and made free, merozoites along with haemozoin are released in to the plasma inducing fever to the person because haemozoin is a toxin. Each attack of fever consists of three stages: i. Cold stage: In this stage, patient feels much cold with shivering and chattering teeth. ii. Hot stage: As the cold stage or chill subsides, the body temperature increases up to 106°F with a terrible headache. iii. Sweating stage: Patient sweats profusely in this stage due to lowering of temperature.
Temperature becomes normal until the next attack of fever (in 48 hours).
Other symptoms of malaria are anaemia, haemolysis, splenomegaly (enlargement of spleen) etc.

Control measures of mosquito 1. Adult mosquitoes can be destructed by various methods like manual killing, using traps, fumigation, spraying insecticides etc. 2. Swampy areas, marshes, stagnant water such as pools ponds ditches should be removed from human dwelling areas as they are the breeding places of mosquito. 3. Open drains should be closed. 4. Tin cans, bucket, unused tyre, barrels etc. should be removed because they serve as breeding places for mosquito. 5. Bushes and shrubs should be cleared off. 6. Destructing the breeding places, such as water reservoir of mosquito by spraying oil, kerosene, and other chemicals. 7. Biological control of mosquito can be done by the help of predator fishes like Gambusia, trout, stickle back in ponds, pools, ditches and other water reservoirs.
